result.title: Auditable Authorization for LLM Agents: Empirical Evidence Across Model, Harness, and Workflow Layers
result.summary:
Human approval provides effective control only if rejected work stops and authorized work completes. We formalize refusal safety and bounded authorization completeness, and audit three execution boundaries: the model selects a call, the harness schedules and resumes it, and the workflow routes the decision to a protected effect. Paired decisions, exact traces, and native business-state witnesses support experiments with three models, five prompt arms, four runtime approval designs, two additional framework replays, and 100 public workflow sources.
  The paired model panel leaves seven of 300 approvals unfinished despite zero denied effects; parallel confirmation loses an approved branch in three tasks per model, restoration omits 336/672 CrewAI approvals, and four of 59 comparable n8n workflows execute after Reject. Comparing intent, generated calls, dispatch, and native effects identifies the first observable divergence and its repair target. This yields a practical audit contract that makes both refusal safety and authorization completeness independently verifiable, converting human approval from a procedural formality into an enforceable control boundary between intent and real-world effect.

AI.brief_summary: 论文形式化 LLM agent 审批中的「拒绝安全」与「有界授权完整性」，在模型、harness 与 workflow 三个执行边界上做配对实验与轨迹审计，定位「意图→生成调用→调度→真实效应」链条中首个可观测分叉点，并提出可独立验证的审计契约。
AI.relevance_reason: 该审计契约「上游已批准的决策是否真正传导到下游效应」的思路，可供核查 LVR 中「答案是否实际使用 latent 内容」的贡献分配与证据丢失定位；但其对象是 agent 授权与工作流，与视觉推理无直接联系。
